title: Two observed_terminal tests from w-814b spin forever on Windows after their fixture root is deleted
outcome: observed_terminal_exact_failure_does_not_resurrect_after_worktree_loss_or_boot and observed_terminal_exact_pass_does_not_resurrect_after_worktree_loss_or_boot finish on Windows as they do on Linux, and a Windows run of the Rust suite no longer hangs on them.
acceptance: The cause is established from source and a discriminating observation, separating what was read or run from what is inferred, and it is stated whether the production path (not only the fixture) can resolve a Git directory outside the lost worktree, such as the real repository's .git. If production can, that is fixed as a product defect, not only in the test.
Nothing in the original or the repaired run writes to the real repository's .git or working tree; this is checked and recorded.
The repair passes both tests on Windows and Linux without a retry, a larger timeout, a skipped or weakened assertion, and the original hung runs (test-604e9116, test-202a8385) stay on record.
The required review pair and the exact-input full gate pass, including a Windows run of the affected Rust tests.

completion.summary: Landed missing-root identity repair ed2b5e4d after clear review pair, Windows affected coverage and exact-tree five-stage FULL. Original terminal-loss tests now pass on Windows and Linux; failed originals and bounded write-audit limits preserved.
